Intro to CS · Teacher Guide

Facilitator's Guide: Code & Web

Ten lessons that move from block coding and debugging into one published HTML/CSS page.

What students make

Students finish with a web page they structured in HTML, styled in CSS, tested, published, and explained during a short presentation. Days 1 through 6 build the skills. Days 7 and 9 are mini-project checkpoints. Day 10 is the 100-point major assessment.

Sequence

  1. Day 1: sequence and first block program
  2. Day 2: student-choice Hour of Code
  3. Day 3: debugging and a three-bug log
  4. Day 4: input, storage, processing, and output
  5. Day 5: inspect web pages and write first HTML
  6. Day 6: headings, lists, and document structure
  7. Day 7: publish an HTML mini-project
  8. Day 8: selectors, properties, values, and readable CSS
  9. Day 9: style and republish the mini-project
  10. Day 10: presentation, peer feedback, and next steps in CS
  11. Xello: complete the Skills lesson

Code.org check for 2027

The exact Express 2025 and CS Discoveries 2026 lesson links in this module returned successfully on August 9, 2026. Code.org says CS Discoveries remains accessible, but recommends AI Discoveries for schools planning 2026-27 courses.

This module keeps CS Discoveries because the S&S specifically maps the two-week sequence to its computing and web-development lessons. Before teaching, open every lesson from a student account. If the district moves to AI Discoveries, remap the full sequence and its evidence instead of swapping isolated URLs.

Setup

  • Create a Code.org class section and give students its join process before Day 1.
  • Test Web Lab sharing from a student account before Day 7. The published link must open outside the student account.
  • Decide whether students will write reflections in English, Spanish, or either language. The page provides both sets of directions.
  • Make sure screenshots are readable. Students may use the Chromebook screenshot shortcut instead of photographing the screen.
  • Check the Day 10 rubric before the unit begins. Its four categories are the published page, walkthrough, gallery feedback, and reflection.
  • Confirm that Xello's Skills lesson is available through ClassLink and that students have the required saved-career work from the earlier check-in.

What to look for while students work

  • A student who is not signed in may lose progress.
  • A screenshot proves completion, not understanding. Ask students to name the bug, sequence, input/output relationship, or HTML choice shown in their work.
  • Days 7, 9, and 10 depend on a working published link. Have students test it in a new tab before submission.
  • Do not let color and font choices hide broken HTML. Structure comes before style.

Official curriculum reference: Code.org Computer Science Discoveries

Intro to CS · Day 1 of 10

Your First Code

Build a sequence, run it, and use the result to revise your instructions.

  • Tool: Code.org Express, Lesson 1
  • Time: one class period
  • Turn in: progress screenshot and reflection
  • English
  • Español

English

Words for today: algorithm · program · sequence

What to do

  1. Sign in through your teacher's Code.org section so your progress saves. Open Programming with Angry Birds.
  2. Before moving a block, say the route in ordinary words. That ordered plan is the algorithm.
  3. Build the plan with blocks and run it. If the result is wrong, change one block and run it again.
  4. At the end of class, capture the lesson progress screen with your completed levels visible.

If your code is not working

  1. Read the instruction at the top of the level again.
  2. Run the code after one change so you know which change mattered.
  3. Use the built-in hint, then show your teacher the level and what you already tried.

Before you submit

  • Upload a readable progress screenshot.
  • In the submission comment, complete the reflection below.

Reflection

Write 2 or 3 sentences: "The computer did something I did not expect when I ____. I figured out it was because ____."

Word bank: algorithm · program · sequence · block · order · run

Español

Palabras de hoy: algorithm (algoritmo) · program (programa) · sequence (secuencia)

Qué hacer

  1. Inicia sesión en la sección de Code.org de tu maestro para guardar tu avance. Abre Programming with Angry Birds.
  2. Antes de mover un bloque, di la ruta con palabras comunes. Ese plan ordenado es el algoritmo.
  3. Construye el plan con bloques y ejecútalo. Si el resultado no funciona, cambia un bloque y vuelve a ejecutarlo.
  4. Al final de la clase, toma una captura de la pantalla de avance con tus niveles completados visibles.

Si tu código no funciona

  1. Vuelve a leer la instrucción que aparece arriba del nivel.
  2. Ejecuta el código después de un solo cambio para saber cuál cambio importó.
  3. Usa la pista del nivel. Después, muéstrale a tu maestro el nivel y lo que ya intentaste.

Antes de entregar

  • Sube una captura legible de tu avance.
  • En el comentario de la entrega, completa la reflexión de abajo.

Reflexión

Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones: "La computadora hizo algo que no esperaba cuando ____. Descubrí que fue porque ____."

Banco de palabras: algoritmo · programa · secuencia · bloque · orden · ejecutar

Intro to CS · Day 2 of 10

Hour of Code

Choose one activity and find the coding ideas inside it.

  • Tool: Hour of Code
  • Time: one class period
  • Turn in: certificate or completion screenshot and reflection
  • English
  • Español

English

Words for today: loop · event · command

What to do

  1. Open the Hour of Code activity list. Choose one activity marked for your grade range.
  2. Try it for five minutes. If the reading level or coding level does not fit, choose a different activity.
  3. Work through the activity on your own screen. Notice one place where order matters, a loop repeats instructions, or an event starts an action.
  4. Capture the certificate, completion screen, or finished project when you reach the end.

If your code is not working

  1. Read the instruction at the top of the level again.
  2. Run the code after one change so you know which change mattered.
  3. Use the built-in hint, then show your teacher the level and what you already tried.

Before you submit

  • Upload a certificate, completion screen, or finished-project screenshot.
  • In the submission comment, name the activity and complete the reflection.

Español

Qué hacer

  1. Abre la lista de actividades de Hour of Code. Escoge una actividad marcada para tus grados.
  2. Pruébala durante cinco minutos. Si el nivel de lectura o programación no te queda bien, escoge otra actividad.
  3. Trabaja la actividad en tu propia pantalla. Busca un lugar donde el orden importe, un bucle repita instrucciones o un evento inicie una acción.
  4. Toma una captura del certificado, la pantalla de finalización o el proyecto terminado.

Si tu código no funciona

  1. Vuelve a leer la instrucción que aparece arriba del nivel.
  2. Ejecuta el código después de un solo cambio para saber cuál cambio importó.
  3. Usa la pista del nivel. Después, muéstrale a tu maestro el nivel y lo que ya intentaste.

Antes de entregar

  • Sube una captura del certificado, la pantalla de finalización o el proyecto terminado.
  • En el comentario, nombra la actividad y completa la reflexión.

Intro to CS · Day 3 of 10

Debugging Detective

Find the difference between what the code should do and what it actually does.

  • Tool: Code.org Express, Lesson 2
  • Time: one class period
  • Turn in: progress screenshot, three-bug log, and reflection
  • English
  • Español

English

Words for today: bug · debug · test

What to do

  1. Sign in through your teacher's Code.org section. Open Debugging in Maze.
  2. For each puzzle, predict what the current blocks will do before you press Run.
  3. Change one block, test, and compare the result with your prediction.
  4. Keep a three-bug log. For each bug, record what happened, what you changed, and how the next test changed the result.
  5. Capture the lesson progress screen at the end of class.

If your code is not working

  1. Read the instruction at the top of the level again.
  2. Run the code after one change so you know which change mattered.
  3. Use the built-in hint, then show your teacher the level and what you already tried.

Before you submit

  • Upload the progress screenshot and the three-bug log.
  • In the submission comment, complete the reflection.

Reflection

Write 2 or 3 sentences: "The bug that took the longest was ____. I found it by ____."

Word bank: bug · debug · test · predict · result · change

Español

Palabras de hoy: bug (error) · debug (depurar) · test (probar)

Qué hacer

  1. Inicia sesión en la sección de Code.org de tu maestro. Abre Debugging in Maze.
  2. En cada rompecabezas, predice qué harán los bloques actuales antes de presionar Run.
  3. Cambia un bloque, prueba y compara el resultado con tu predicción.
  4. Mantén un registro de tres errores. Para cada uno, anota qué pasó, qué cambiaste y cómo cambió el resultado en la siguiente prueba.
  5. Toma una captura de la pantalla de avance al final de la clase.

Si tu código no funciona

  1. Vuelve a leer la instrucción que aparece arriba del nivel.
  2. Ejecuta el código después de un solo cambio para saber cuál cambio importó.
  3. Usa la pista del nivel. Después, muéstrale a tu maestro el nivel y lo que ya intentaste.

Antes de entregar

  • Sube la captura de avance y el registro de tres errores.
  • En el comentario, completa la reflexión.

Reflexión

Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones: "El error que más tardé en resolver fue ____. Lo encontré al ____."

Banco de palabras: error · depurar · probar · predecir · resultado · cambio

Intro to CS · Day 4 of 10

How Computers Think

Map how a device takes in information, works with it, and produces a result.

  • Tool: CS Discoveries Unit 1, Lessons 4 and 6
  • Time: one class period
  • Turn in: device map and reflection
  • English
  • Español

English

Words for today: input · storage · processing · output

What to do

  1. Open What is a Computer? and complete the assigned levels.
  2. Open Processing and complete the assigned levels.
  3. Choose one device you use. Make a four-part map showing its input, what it stores, how it processes information, and its output.
  4. Check the map by tracing one real action from start to finish. Example: press a key, the device processes the signal, and a letter appears.

If your code is not working

  1. Name the exact action you are tracing.
  2. If two boxes sound the same, ask what information enters and what result comes out.
  3. Show the map to your teacher before submitting if one section is still blank.

Before you submit

  • Upload a readable photo, scan, or digital copy of the four-part device map.
  • In the submission comment, complete the reflection.

Reflection

Write 2 or 3 sentences: "The input on my device is ____. The device processes it by ____, which produces ____ as the output."

Word bank: input · storage · processing · output · device · information

Español

Palabras de hoy: input (entrada) · storage (almacenamiento) · processing (procesamiento) · output (salida)

Qué hacer

  1. Abre What is a Computer? y completa los niveles asignados.
  2. Abre Processing y completa los niveles asignados.
  3. Escoge un dispositivo que uses. Haz un mapa de cuatro partes que muestre su entrada, lo que almacena, cómo procesa la información y su salida.
  4. Revisa el mapa siguiendo una acción real de principio a fin. Ejemplo: presionas una tecla, el dispositivo procesa la señal y aparece una letra.

Si tu código no funciona

  1. Nombra la acción exacta que estás siguiendo.
  2. Si dos cuadros dicen casi lo mismo, pregunta qué información entra y qué resultado sale.
  3. Muéstrale el mapa a tu maestro antes de entregar si todavía falta una sección.

Antes de entregar

  • Sube una foto legible, un escaneo o una copia digital del mapa de cuatro partes.
  • En el comentario, completa la reflexión.

Reflexión

Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones: "La entrada de mi dispositivo es ____. El dispositivo la procesa al ____, lo que produce ____ como salida."

Banco de palabras: entrada · almacenamiento · procesamiento · salida · dispositivo · información

Intro to CS · Day 5 of 10

Explore Websites and Start HTML

Look behind a web page, then write the tags that give a page its structure.

  • Tool: CS Discoveries Unit 2, Lessons 1 and 2
  • Time: one class period
  • Turn in: first HTML page screenshot and reflection
  • English
  • Español

English

Words for today: HTML · tag · element

What to do

  1. Open Exploring Web Pages. Complete the assigned levels and notice how the code connects to what appears in the preview.
  2. Open Intro to HTML. Complete the assigned levels.
  3. In Web Lab, write a heading and a paragraph. Change one piece of text and run the page again so you can see which code controls it.
  4. Capture the code and the preview together. The screenshot should make both readable.

If your code is not working

  1. Check that each opening tag has the closing tag the lesson expects.
  2. Look for a missing angle bracket if code appears as ordinary text on the page.
  3. Change one line at a time, then compare the preview.

Before you submit

  • Upload one screenshot showing your HTML and its page preview.
  • In the submission comment, complete the reflection.

Reflection

Write 2 or 3 sentences: "The ____ tag controls ____. I know because when I changed ____, the page ____."

Word bank: HTML · tag · element · heading · paragraph · preview

Español

Palabras de hoy: HTML · tag (etiqueta) · element (elemento)

Qué hacer

  1. Abre Exploring Web Pages. Completa los niveles asignados y observa cómo el código se conecta con lo que aparece en la vista previa.
  2. Abre Intro to HTML. Completa los niveles asignados.
  3. En Web Lab, escribe un encabezado y un párrafo. Cambia una parte del texto y vuelve a ejecutar la página para ver qué código la controla.
  4. Toma una captura del código y la vista previa juntos. Los dos deben poder leerse.

Si tu código no funciona

  1. Revisa que cada etiqueta de apertura tenga la etiqueta de cierre que pide la lección.
  2. Busca un signo de menor o mayor que falte si el código aparece como texto común en la página.
  3. Cambia una línea a la vez y compara la vista previa.

Antes de entregar

  • Sube una captura que muestre tu HTML y la vista previa de la página.
  • En el comentario, completa la reflexión.

Reflexión

Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones: "La etiqueta ____ controla ____. Lo sé porque cuando cambié ____, la página ____."

resource.body:
Intro to CS · Day 6 of 10

HTML Headings and Structure

Use headings and lists to make the page's organization visible in the code and on the screen.

  • Tool: CS Discoveries Unit 2, Lesson 3
  • Time: one class period
  • Turn in: structured-page screenshot, outline, and reflection
  • English
  • Español

English

Words for today: heading · list · nesting

What to do

  1. Open Headings and Lists and complete the assigned levels.
  2. Make a short outline for your page: one page title, at least two section headings, and the points that belong under each section.
  3. Build the outline in Web Lab with one h1, two or more h2 headings, paragraphs, and at least one list.
  4. Check the nesting. The content for each section should sit under the heading that names it.
  5. Capture the code and preview together so both are readable.

If your code is not working

  1. Compare the heading order in your outline with the order in your HTML.
  2. If a list does not work, check the opening and closing tags around the list and each item.
  3. Change one tag at a time and watch the preview.

Before you submit

  • Upload the page screenshot and your short outline.
  • In the submission comment, complete the reflection.

Reflection

Write 2 or 3 sentences: "I used my h1 for ____. My h2 headings divide the page into ____ and ____."

Word bank: heading · list · nesting · h1 · h2 · section · outline

Español

Palabras de hoy: heading (encabezado) · list (lista) · nesting (anidación)

Qué hacer

  1. Abre Headings and Lists y completa los niveles asignados.
  2. Haz un esquema corto para tu página: un título, al menos dos encabezados de sección y los puntos que van en cada sección.
  3. Construye el esquema en Web Lab con un h1, dos o más encabezados h2, párrafos y al menos una lista.
  4. Revisa la anidación. El contenido de cada sección debe quedar debajo del encabezado que la nombra.
  5. Toma una captura del código y la vista previa juntos para que los dos se puedan leer.

Si tu código no funciona

  1. Compara el orden de los encabezados en tu esquema con el orden del HTML.
  2. Si una lista no funciona, revisa las etiquetas de apertura y cierre de la lista y de cada elemento.
  3. Cambia una etiqueta a la vez y observa la vista previa.

Antes de entregar

  • Sube la captura de la página y tu esquema corto.
  • En el comentario, completa la reflexión.

Reflexión

Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones: "Usé mi h1 para ____. Mis encabezados h2 dividen la página en ____ y ____."

Banco de palabras: encabezado · lista · anidación · h1 · h2 · sección · esquema

Intro to CS · Day 7 of 10

Mini-Project: Build Your HTML Page

Plan one page, build its structure, and publish a link another person can open.

  • Tool: CS Discoveries Unit 2, Lesson 5
  • Time: one class period
  • Turn in: published link, screenshot, and reflection
  • English
  • Español

English

Words for today: structure · publish · audience

What to do

  1. Open Mini-Project: HTML Web Page and read its directions before building.
  2. Choose a topic you can explain in one page. Plan the title, at least two sections, and one useful list.
  3. Build one h1, at least two h2 headings, at least four paragraphs, and at least one ordered or unordered list.
  4. Check that every tag closes and that the preview follows your plan. Ask a classmate to name the page topic after a ten-second look.
  5. Use Share to publish. Open the link in a new tab and make sure it works before submitting.

If your code is not working

  1. Return to your plan and build one section at a time.
  2. If a large part of the page looks wrong, inspect the tag immediately before that section.
  3. Test the published link in a new tab before asking for help.

Before you submit

  • Upload one screenshot showing the finished page.
  • Paste the working published link in the submission comment.
  • Complete the reflection in the same comment.

Reflection

Write 2 or 3 sentences: "My page is for ____. I organized it into ____ because ____."

Word bank: structure · publish · audience · heading · paragraph · list

Español

Palabras de hoy: structure (estructura) · publish (publicar) · audience (audiencia)

Qué hacer

  1. Abre Mini-Project: HTML Web Page y lee las instrucciones antes de construir.
  2. Escoge un tema que puedas explicar en una página. Planea el título, al menos dos secciones y una lista útil.
  3. Construye un h1, al menos dos encabezados h2, al menos cuatro párrafos y una lista ordenada o sin orden.
  4. Revisa que cada etiqueta cierre y que la vista previa siga tu plan. Pídele a un compañero que identifique el tema después de mirar la página durante diez segundos.
  5. Usa Share para publicar. Abre el enlace en una pestaña nueva y confirma que funcione antes de entregar.

Si tu código no funciona

  1. Regresa a tu plan y construye una sección a la vez.
  2. Si una parte grande se ve mal, revisa la etiqueta justo antes de esa sección.
  3. Prueba el enlace publicado en una pestaña nueva antes de pedir ayuda.

Antes de entregar

  • Sube una captura de la página terminada.
  • Pega el enlace publicado que funciona en el comentario de la entrega.
  • Completa la reflexión en el mismo comentario.

Reflexión

Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones: "Mi página es para ____. La organicé en ____ porque ____."

Banco de palabras: estructura · publicar · audiencia · encabezado · párrafo · lista

Intro to CS · Day 8 of 10

Style with CSS

Use selectors, properties, and values to change the page without changing its HTML structure.

  • Tool: CS Discoveries Unit 2, Lessons 6 and 9
  • Time: one class period
  • Turn in: before-and-after screenshot and reflection
  • English
  • Español

English

Words for today: selector · property · value

What to do

  1. Open Styling Text with CSS and complete the assigned levels.
  2. Open your Day 7 page. Save or capture a before view.
  3. Add one CSS rule at a time. Start with a selector, add one property and value, then check the preview before adding another rule.
  4. Style at least a heading and paragraph. Keep enough contrast between the text and background to read every word.
  5. If time remains, use Styling Elements with CSS to try a border, padding, or margin.
  6. Capture an after view from the same part of the page.

If your code is not working

  1. Check the punctuation in the CSS rule, including the braces, colon, and semicolon.
  2. Make one change and refresh the preview before changing another property.
  3. If the text disappears, check the text and background colors.

Before you submit

  • Upload the before-and-after views in one file or two readable images.
  • In the submission comment, name one selector, property, and value you used, then complete the reflection.

Reflection

Write 2 or 3 sentences: "I used the selector ____. I changed the ____ property to ____ because ____."

Word bank: selector · property · value · contrast · font · background

Español

Palabras de hoy: selector · property (propiedad) · value (valor)

Qué hacer

  1. Abre Styling Text with CSS y completa los niveles asignados.
  2. Abre tu página del Día 7. Guarda o toma una captura del antes.
  3. Agrega una regla de CSS a la vez. Empieza con un selector, agrega una propiedad y un valor, y revisa la vista previa antes de agregar otra regla.
  4. Estiliza al menos un encabezado y un párrafo. Mantén suficiente contraste entre el texto y el fondo para leer cada palabra.
  5. Si queda tiempo, usa Styling Elements with CSS para probar un borde, padding o margin.
  6. Toma una captura del después desde la misma parte de la página.

Si tu código no funciona

  1. Revisa la puntuación de la regla de CSS, incluyendo las llaves, los dos puntos y el punto y coma.
  2. Haz un cambio y actualiza la vista previa antes de cambiar otra propiedad.
  3. Si desaparece el texto, revisa los colores del texto y del fondo.

Antes de entregar

  • Sube las vistas de antes y después en un archivo o en dos imágenes legibles.
  • En el comentario, nombra un selector, una propiedad y un valor que usaste. Después completa la reflexión.

Reflexión

Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones: "Usé el selector ____. Cambié la propiedad ____ a ____ porque ____."

Banco de palabras: selector · propiedad · valor · contraste · fuente · fondo

Intro to CS · Day 9 of 10

Mini-Project: Style Your Page

Make a small set of design choices that help a reader understand the page.

  • Tool: CS Discoveries Unit 2, Lesson 10
  • Time: one class period
  • Turn in: styled-page screenshot, published link, and reflection
  • English
  • Español

English

Words for today: rule · design · contrast

What to do

  1. Open Mini-Project: Adding Style to a Web Page and read the requirements.
  2. Choose two or three colors and decide what the reader should notice first. Write those choices down before editing CSS.
  3. Add at least six CSS rules. Include rules for headings, paragraphs, and the page background; one font-family or font-size; and one border, padding, or margin.
  4. Check the page at normal Chromebook size. Every word should remain readable, and the headings should still show the page structure.
  5. Ask a classmate to look for ten seconds and tell you what the page is about. Revise one thing based on that test.
  6. Publish again and test the link in a new tab.

If your code is not working

  1. Compare the page with the design choices you wrote before coding.
  2. If several rules stop working, inspect the punctuation immediately before the first broken rule.
  3. Use a simple light or dark background if contrast is getting hard to control.

Before you submit

  • Upload a screenshot of the styled page.
  • Paste the tested published link in the submission comment.
  • Complete the reflection in the same comment.

Reflection

Write 2 or 3 sentences: "I wanted the page to feel ____, so I chose ____. After a classmate tested it, I changed ____."

Word bank: rule · design · contrast · selector · property · font · background

Español

Palabras de hoy: rule (regla) · design (diseño) · contrast (contraste)

Qué hacer

  1. Abre Mini-Project: Adding Style to a Web Page y lee los requisitos.
  2. Escoge dos o tres colores y decide qué debe notar primero el lector. Escribe esas decisiones antes de editar el CSS.
  3. Agrega al menos seis reglas de CSS. Incluye reglas para encabezados, párrafos y el fondo; un font-family o font-size; y un border, padding o margin.
  4. Revisa la página al tamaño normal de la Chromebook. Cada palabra debe poder leerse y los encabezados deben mostrar la estructura.
  5. Pídele a un compañero que mire la página durante diez segundos y te diga de qué trata. Revisa una cosa basándote en esa prueba.
  6. Publica de nuevo y prueba el enlace en una pestaña nueva.

Si tu código no funciona

  1. Compara la página con las decisiones de diseño que escribiste antes de programar.
  2. Si varias reglas dejan de funcionar, revisa la puntuación justo antes de la primera regla rota.
  3. Usa un fondo claro u oscuro sencillo si el contraste se vuelve difícil de controlar.

Antes de entregar

  • Sube una captura de la página estilizada.
  • Pega el enlace publicado y probado en el comentario.
  • Completa la reflexión en el mismo comentario.

Reflexión

Escribe 2 o 3 oraciones: "Quería que la página se sintiera ____, así que escogí ____. Después de la prueba de un compañero, cambié ____."

Banco de palabras: regla · diseño · contraste · selector · propiedad · fuente · fondo

Intro to CS · Day 10 of 10

Present Your Web Page

Explain what you built, how you debugged it, and what you want to learn next.

  • Tool: Web Lab and class gallery walk
  • Time: one class period
  • Turn in: published link, walkthrough, peer feedback, and reflection
  • English
  • Español

English

Words for today: feedback · pathway · publish

What to do

  1. Open the Day 9 page and test its published link in a new tab.
  2. Prepare a 90-second walkthrough: name the page and audience, point to one part you built, explain one bug you fixed, and explain one CSS choice.
  3. Present live or record the walkthrough with Canvas, following your teacher's direction.
  4. Visit at least three classmates' pages. For each one, write two specific things that work and one change the student could make in about ten minutes.
  5. Review the CS Discoveries topics. Choose one thing you want to learn next and connect it to a project or career.

If your code is not working

  1. Use an index card with the four walkthrough points if you need it.
  2. Feedback should name a heading, color, section, link, or other visible part of the page.
  3. If the link fails, republish it and test it before submitting.

Before you submit

  • Upload or record the 90-second walkthrough.
  • Paste the working published link in the submission comment.
  • Follow your teacher's process for turning in the feedback you wrote for three classmates.
  • Complete the reflection in the submission comment. Check the rubric before submitting.

Reflection

Write 3 or 4 sentences: "Before this unit, I could not ____. Now I can ____. Next I want to learn ____ because ____."

Word bank: feedback · pathway · HTML · CSS · debug · publish · audience

Español

Palabras de hoy: feedback (retroalimentación) · pathway (trayectoria) · publish (publicar)

Qué hacer

  1. Abre la página del Día 9 y prueba el enlace publicado en una pestaña nueva.
  2. Prepara una explicación de 90 segundos: nombra la página y su audiencia, señala una parte que construiste, explica un error que corregiste y explica una decisión de CSS.
  3. Presenta en vivo o graba la explicación con Canvas, según la instrucción de tu maestro.
  4. Visita las páginas de al menos tres compañeros. Para cada una, escribe dos cosas específicas que funcionan y un cambio que la persona podría hacer en unos diez minutos.
  5. Revisa los temas de CS Discoveries. Escoge algo que quieras aprender después y conéctalo con un proyecto o una carrera.

Si tu código no funciona

  1. Usa una tarjeta con los cuatro puntos de la explicación si la necesitas.
  2. La retroalimentación debe nombrar un encabezado, color, sección, enlace u otra parte visible de la página.
  3. Si el enlace falla, vuelve a publicar y pruébalo antes de entregar.

Antes de entregar

  • Sube o graba la explicación de 90 segundos.
  • Pega el enlace publicado que funciona en el comentario.
  • Sigue el proceso de tu maestro para entregar la retroalimentación que escribiste para tres compañeros.
  • Completa la reflexión en el comentario. Revisa la rúbrica antes de entregar.

Reflexión

Escribe 3 o 4 oraciones: "Antes de esta unidad, no podía ____. Ahora puedo ____. Después quiero aprender ____ porque ____."

Banco de palabras: retroalimentación · trayectoria · HTML · CSS · depurar · publicar · audiencia

resource.body:
■ GAME DESIGN • FACILITATOR’S GUIDE ■

VIDEO GAME DESIGN

Two class periods in MakeCode Arcade: build from a tutorial, then remix it into something nobody else has. Everything you need to run it.

⏱️ 2 class periods🎮 MakeCode Arcade🔒 Microsoft sign-in required🏆 Make: 2 tutorials, then a remix

RUN SHEET

Both lessons are self-contained Canvas assignments with the full lesson inside — hook, word bank, numbered steps, an early-finisher menu, turn-in steps, a reflection stem and an end-of-class checklist, in English and Spanish tabs. Lesson 2 depends on Lesson 1: students remix a game they built the class before.

Module itemWhat happensDeliverable
LESSON 01: SKILLMAPSign-in day and first build. Students open the MakeCode Arcade skillmap, sign in with their school Microsoft account, and finish two tutorial paths off the pink puzzle pieces. The sign-in is step one for a reason — without it nothing saves. Ends with a screenshot upload and a reflection in the comments.Screenshot of 2 completed pieces
Full class period
LESSON 02: REMIXStudents reopen one of their skillmap games from My Projects, rename it, and add two or more features of their own — new enemy, power-up, second level, score multiplier, custom sprite, sound effect. They test after every single change. The reflection asks them to compare remixing against building from scratch.Remixed game + 2 features named
Full class period

🔒 THE SIGN-IN IS THE LESSON’S SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE

MakeCode Arcade saves to the account, not to the machine. A student who works a full period signed out has nothing on Lesson 2 day and no game to remix. Walk the room during step 1 and confirm every screen shows a signed-in name before anyone starts a tutorial.

Microsoft — not Google, not Clever, using the school account. On shared laptops, Remember Me stays OFF, and tell students not to clear cookies between the two classes.

MATERIALS + PREP

  • One device per student with Chrome, and the skillmap link ready to push out: arcade.makecode.com/--skillmap. Lesson 2 starts from the plain arcade.makecode.com instead, because students open their own saved projects.
  • Every student’s school Microsoft account confirmed working before Lesson 1. Sort password resets ahead of the period, not during it — this is the one prep item that decides whether the lesson works.
  • Nothing to print, nothing to buy, no class code to generate. The skillmap is open to anyone with the link.
  • Screenshot shortcut on the board. Both lessons are turned in as a screenshot plus a written reflection in the submission comments.

WATCH-FORS

  • This module is the short cut of a longer unit, and it is complete as it stands. Two lessons, sized to the scope and sequence. Lesson 2 looks backward at Lesson 1 and nothing points forward to a Lesson 3, so you can run it as a self-contained two-day block without anything feeling unfinished.
  • The Spanish tab of Lesson 1 is not a translation of the English one. The English tab includes a MakeCode walkthrough. The Spanish tab does not include that video; it has a note showing where a Spanish walkthrough can be added. The Spanish tab also carries the Remember Me off step and a cookies tip the English tab lacks. If your class works in English, say the shared-laptop rule out loud.
  • Early finishers have somewhere to go. Both lessons carry a LEVEL UP menu — a third tutorial or a third feature, and sharing game links with a partner. Point students at it rather than letting the room drift; the sharing step is where the class actually sees each other’s work.

GRADING — 100 POINTS

Lesson 2: Remix is the module’s Major grade, at 100 points, and it is the only item here that moves a grade. Lesson 1: Skillmap is 0 points — it is the practice run that gets students into MakeCode Arcade.

Both lessons already tell students what finished looks like. Lesson 1: signed in, two tutorials done, screenshot uploaded, reflection written. Lesson 2: game renamed, two or more features added and tested, screenshot uploaded, both features named in the comments.

Both items and the module are unpublished. Publish as you go.

■ GAME DESIGN • LESSON 01 OF 02 ■

WELCOME TO MAKECODE ARCADE

Sign in with Microsoft, then complete 2 skillmap tutorials

🎮 Tool
MakeCode Arcade
🔒 Sign in
Microsoft
⏱️ Time
Full class
🏆 Goal
2 skillmaps
  • English
  • Español

🎮 Ready Player One! Today you start a brand new unit: Game Design. You will build real arcade games using code blocks. 

📚 Word Bank

skillmap • tutorial • sprite • block • project • sign in • save

1

SIGN IN WITH MICROSOFT

This is the most important step. If you skip it, your game will not save.

a. Open a new Chrome tab and go to the MakeCode Arcade skillmap (button below)

b. Click the Sign In button in the upper right corner

c. Pick Microsoft (NOT Google, NOT Clever)

d. Use your school Microsoft account (@stu.irvingisd.net)

e. Leave Remember Me OFF (shared laptop!)

🎯 Open this link

👉 arcade.makecode.com/--skillmap

2

CHOOSE YOUR PATH

You will see a map with three pink puzzle pieces on the left side. Each one starts a different game path.

🧩 Pink puzzle piece = tutorial you can start right now

🔒 Locked pieces = unlock after you finish the one before

🏆 Trophy = end of that path

3

COMPLETE 2 SKILLMAP TUTORIALS

Your mission today: finish TWO skillmap tutorials.

Click the top pink puzzle piece to start

Follow the tutorial steps – drag blocks into the workspace

Press the play button to test your game

Finish the first puzzle piece and go back to the map

Start a second pink puzzle piece (any path you want)

⭐ LEVEL UP

Finished early? Pick one:

• Start a 3rd skillmap tutorial

• Hit the Share button and send your game link to a partner

💾 TURN IN

1. Take a screenshot of your skillmap showing 2 completed puzzle pieces

2. Click Start Assignment in Canvas

3. Upload your screenshot

4. Answer the reflection in Comments

💬 REFLECT

In the comments of your submission, finish this sentence in 2-3 sentences:

“After finishing my first 2 skillmap tutorials, I can now ______ in MakeCode Arcade because ______.”

Word Bank

skillmap • tutorial • sprite • block • project • save • code • Microsoft

✅ END OF CLASS

✔ Signed in to MakeCode Arcade with Microsoft

✔ Completed 2 skillmap tutorials

✔ Uploaded screenshot to Canvas

✔ Answered reflection in comments

🎮 ¡Ready Player One! Hoy empiezas una nueva unidad: Diseño de Videojuegos. Vas a crear juegos de arcade reales usando bloques de código. No necesitas experiencia previa – los tutoriales te enseñan paso a paso.

📚 Banco de Palabras

skillmap (mapa de habilidades) • tutorial • sprite • block (bloque) • project (proyecto) • sign in (iniciar sesión) • save (guardar)

1

INICIA SESIÓN CON MICROSOFT

Este es el paso más importante. Si no inicias sesión, tu juego no se va a guardar.

a. Abre una pestaña nueva en Chrome y ve al skillmap de MakeCode Arcade (botón abajo)

b. Haz clic en Sign In en la esquina superior derecha

c. Elige Microsoft (NO Google, NO Clever)

d. Usa tu cuenta Microsoft de la escuela (la misma con que entras a la laptop)

e. Deja Remember Me APAGADO (¡laptop compartida!)

🎯 Abre este enlace

👉 arcade.makecode.com/--skillmap

💡 Tip: No borres las cookies o pierdes tu progreso. ¡Guarda el enlace como favorito!

2

ELIGE TU CAMINO

Vas a ver un mapa con tres piezas rosas de rompecabezas al lado izquierdo. Cada una empieza un camino diferente.

🧩 Pieza rosa = tutorial que puedes empezar ahora

🔒 Piezas con candado = se desbloquean después de terminar la anterior

🏆 Trofeo = final de ese camino

3

COMPLETA 2 TUTORIALES

Tu misión de hoy: terminar DOS tutoriales del skillmap.

Haz clic en la pieza rosa de arriba para empezar

Sigue los pasos – arrastra los bloques al área de trabajo

Presiona el botón de play para probar tu juego

Termina la primera pieza y regresa al mapa

Empieza otra pieza rosa (cualquier camino que quieras)

🎬 Video de guía

Ms. Lucero va a poner un video de MakeCode Arcade aquí

⭐ LEVEL UP

¿Terminaste temprano? Elige uno:

• Empieza un 3er tutorial

• Presiona Share y mandale tu juego a un compañero

💾 ENTREGA

1. Toma una captura de pantalla del skillmap con 2 piezas completadas

2. Haz clic en Start Assignment en Canvas

3. Sube tu captura de pantalla

4. Contesta la reflexión en Comments

💬 REFLEXIÓN

En los comments de tu entrega, termina esta oración en 2-3 oraciones (en inglés):

(En los comentarios de tu entrega, completa esta oración en inglés.)

“After finishing my first 2 skillmap tutorials, I can now ______ in MakeCode Arcade because ______.”

Word Bank / Banco de Palabras

skillmap (mapa) • tutorial • sprite • block (bloque) • project (proyecto) • save (guardar) • code (código) • Microsoft

✅ AL TERMINAR LA CLASE

✔ Sesión iniciada con cuenta Microsoft

✔ 2 tutoriales del skillmap completados

✔ Captura de pantalla subida a Canvas

✔ Reflexión contestada en comments

■ GAME DESIGN • LESSON 02 OF 02 ■

GAME REMIX CHALLENGE

Take a game you built and make it yours by adding 2+ new features

🎮 Tool
MakeCode Arcade
📂 Start With
Your skillmap game
⏱️ Time
Full class
🏆 Goal
2+ new features
  • English
  • Español

🔥 Level 2 unlocked! You built a tutorial game. Now you are going to remix it by adding your own twist so no two games in class look alike.

📚 Word Bank

Remix – changing, adding, or rearranging parts of a project to make it your own

Conditional – a block that checks if something is true or false, then runs different code (if/then)

1

OPEN YOUR GAME

a. Go to arcade.makecode.com and sign in with Microsoft

b. Find My Projects – pick one of the skillmap games you finished last class

c. Rename it to "[Your Name] Remix" so we can tell it apart

2

PICK 2 FEATURES TO ADD

Choose at least 2 from the menu below (or invent your own):

💩 New enemy type – different sprite, speed, or damage

⭐ Power-up – speed boost, extra life, shield

🎮 Second level – new background after a score goal

💯 Score multiplier – double or triple points on a combo

🎨 Custom sprite – draw your own character in the pixel editor

🎵 Sound effect – play a sound when something happens

3

BUILD & TEST

Drag blocks from the toolbox to add your features (try if / then conditionals for power-ups)

Press play after each change – test one feature at a time

Something broken? Undo (Ctrl+Z) and try a different block. Ask a neighbor before asking Ms. Lucero.

⭐ LEVEL UP

Finished early? Pick one:

• Add a 3rd or 4th feature

• Hit Share and swap game links with a partner

💾 TURN IN

1. Take a screenshot of your remixed game (gameplay view)

2. Click Start Assignment in Canvas

3. Upload your screenshot

4. In Comments: list the 2 features you added and why

💬 REFLECT

In the comments of your submission, answer both parts:

How is remixing an existing game different from building one from scratch? Which do you think teaches you more, and why?

Word Bank

remix • conditional • sprite • feature • scratch • modify

✅ END OF CLASS

✔ Opened a skillmap game and renamed it

✔ Added 2+ new features

✔ Tested the game after each change

✔ Uploaded screenshot + answered reflection in comments

🔥 ¡Nivel 2 desbloqueado! Ya construiste un juego del tutorial. Ahora vas a hacerle un remix – ponle tu propio estilo para que ningún juego en la clase se vea igual.

📚 Banco de Palabras

Remix – cambiar, agregar o reorganizar partes de un proyecto para hacerlo tuyo

Conditional (condicional) – un bloque que revisa si algo es verdadero o falso, y corre código diferente según el resultado (if/then)

1

ABRE TU JUEGO

a. Ve a arcade.makecode.com y inicia sesión con Microsoft

b. Busca My Projects – elige uno de los juegos del skillmap que terminaste la clase pasada

2

ELIGE 2 CARACTERÍSTICAS

Escoge al menos 2 del menú (o inventa las tuyas):

💩 Nuevo enemigo – sprite, velocidad o daño diferente

⭐ Power-up – velocidad extra, vida extra, escudo

🎮 Segundo nivel – nuevo fondo al llegar a cierto puntaje

💯 Multiplicador – puntos dobles o triples en combo

🎨 Sprite personalizado – dibuja tu propio personaje en el editor de pixeles

🎵 Efecto de sonido – reproduce un sonido cuando pasa algo

3

CONSTRUYE Y PRUEBA

Arrastra bloques de la caja de herramientas para agregar tus features (usa if / then para power-ups)

Presiona play después de cada cambio – prueba una cosa a la vez

¿Se rompió algo? Deshaz con Ctrl+Z y prueba otro bloque. Pregúntale a un compañero antes que a Ms. Lucero.

⭐ LEVEL UP

¿Terminaste temprano? Elige uno:

💾 ENTREGA

2. Haz clic en Start Assignment en Canvas

💬 REFLEXIÓN

How is remixing an existing game different from building one from scratch? Which do you think teaches you more, and why?

remix • conditional (condicional) • sprite • feature (característica) • scratch (desde cero) • modify (modificar)

✅ AL TERMINAR LA CLASE

For each Edpuzzle assignment, choose Edit, keep Submission Type: External Tool, choose Find, then Edpuzzle. Select the matching lesson from My Content, save, and test it in Student View.

Open Edpuzzle's Canvas setup guide. If you are not using Edpuzzle, the original-video links above let you run the lesson without the integration.

Facilitator’s Guide · SW4 · AIR Unit 0

Facilitator’s Guide: AIR Unit 0 — Intro to AI

Where the AIR story starts: a robot that needs instructions, and a machine you teach by example.

📅 4 lessons📺 EdPuzzle · Teachable Machine🏆 30 points in the module

The unit at a glance

Module itemWhat happensPoints
Lesson 1: Bon Voyage, Robot!
Learn: Lesson 1 Bon Voyage, Robot!The lesson video, posted for rewatching. The page says it plainly: do it in the EdPuzzle, this copy is only for going back.0
EdPuzzle | Bon Voyage, Robot! (AIR)The graded version of the same video, with questions inside the player. This is the one students actually complete.5
Activity: Lesson 1 Bon Voyage, Robot!The Lesson 1 activity, built around a second video. Submits as a link or an upload.5
Lesson 2: Permission to Come Aboard with Algorithms
EdPuzzle | Permission to Come Aboard with AlgorithmsWatch first. Blank page in Canvas — the launch button is the item.5
Lesson 2: Permission to Come Aboard with AlgorithmsThe built lesson. Students read the map of The Docks and write an algorithm in pseudocode to move HorizonBot and four boxes to the ship. The page shows the same maze as pseudocode, Blockly and JavaScript side by side.0
Lesson 3: Smart Machines
EdPuzzle | AIR Lesson 3: Smart MachinesWatch first. The page repeats the warning: do not skip the EdPuzzle.5
Lesson 3: Smart MachinesStudents train a two-class image model in Teachable Machine using two objects they can hold up to a camera, then test where it fails.0
Lesson 5: AIR + Sustainability
EdPuzzle | Learn: AIR Sustainability (Pt 1)Part 1 of the sustainability material. Blank page in Canvas.5
Learn: Lesson 5 AIR + SustainabilityThe interactive lesson launch that closes the unit. Blank page in Canvas — opens in a new tab.0
Closing
Xello Check-in: Education ExperiencesStudents add one education experience with reflections to their Xello timeline and upload a screenshot. Runs last.5

Materials + prep

  • EdPuzzle class code tested. Four of the thirteen items are EdPuzzles and they carry the direct instruction for three of the four lessons.
  • Webcams working, and camera permission allowed in the browser, for Lesson 3. Teachable Machine asks for the camera on load; a blocked camera is the failure students will report as “the site is broken.” The lesson offers uploading images as a fallback.
  • Two small objects per student for Lesson 3 — a ball and an apple is the page’s own example. Have a bin of spares; the students who forget are the ones who need the lesson most.
  • Physical class journals. Where these pages say to write in a journal, they mean the notebook on the desk. There is no Canvas item behind it.
  • Lesson 2 projected. The map of The Docks and the three-language pseudocode comparison are worth reading together before students write anything.

Watch-fors

  • The lesson numbers run 1, 2, 3, then 5. There is no Lesson 4 in this module. Continue directly from Lesson 3 to Lesson 5.
  • Three items open with a blank Canvas page. The two sustainability items and the Lesson 2 EdPuzzle have no description at all; the launch button is the whole item. Normal, and worth one sentence at the start of the unit.
  • The four EdPuzzles carry two-thirds of the module’s points. Each is a 5-point Minor grade, and each page says “Minor Grade,” so the label now matches the gradebook. With the Lesson 1 activity and the Xello check-in at 5 apiece, 20 of the module’s 30 points sit inside EdPuzzle.
  • Lessons 2 and 3 are the two biggest builds in the unit and both are worth 0 points. The algorithm for The Docks and the trained Teachable Machine model are real artifacts. The points sit in the four EdPuzzles, the Lesson 1 activity and the Xello check-in; nothing rides on the two builds themselves.
  • Teachable Machine comes back twice more. Lesson 3 is the first meeting; Image Classification and Machine Learning Week both build on it. Keep the models students train here — being able to point back at their own first model is worth more than a fresh start later.

Grading

Six items carry points, all Minor grades at 5 each: the four EdPuzzles, Activity: Lesson 1 Bon Voyage, Robot! and the Xello Check-in: Education Experiences — 30 points total, and no Major grade in this module. Everything else, including both built lessons and the two Learn launches, is set to 0. The Lesson 1 activity accepts a website link or a file upload; the Xello check-in is a screenshot upload.

resource.body:
⬡ AIR · Intro to AI · Lesson 2 ⬡

PERMISSION TO COME ABOARD

HorizonBot will not move until you write the steps.

📅 Intro to AI · Lesson 2
🛠️ Pseudocode + The Docks
⏱️ ~45 min
📦 An algorithm for 4 boxes
  • English
  • Español

📢 HorizonBot is parked on the dock. Four heavy boxes are scattered across The Docks, and the New Horizon is waiting at the pier. The robot will not move one inch until somebody writes down exactly what to do — step by step. Today that somebody is you.

Today's words

algorithm • pseudocode • computer program • loop • conditional

1

Learn what an algorithm is

Complete the EdPuzzle: Permission to Come Aboard with Algorithms and answer the questions inside the video. You need this before you write anything.

2

See how a plan turns into code

Pseudocode is how programmers pre-write an algorithm: plain language a human can read, but that a computer cannot run yet. Here is the same maze solved three ways — first the plan, then two versions a computer can actually execute.

Pseudocode

Start
Go Forward
Turn Left
Go Forward
Turn Right
Go Forward
End

Blockly

move forward
turn left ↺
move forward
turn right ↻
move forward

JavaScript

moveForward();
turnLeft();
moveForward();
turnRight();
moveForward();

Same steps every time. Only the language changes.

3

Read the map of The Docks

Before you write anything, study the map. Find these four things:

• HorizonBot — the blue robot, on the left side of the dock

• The four boxes — the orange crates scattered across The Docks

• The obstacles — the dark red crates already stacked on the dock floor

• The New Horizon — the ship at the pier on the right, over the water

Ask yourself: how will you get HorizonBot to every box and then to the ship? Is there more than one way to do it?

4

Write your pseudocode algorithm

Your goal: move HorizonBot from its starting spot, through The Docks, pick up all four boxes, and deliver them to the New Horizon. Write your algorithm using only these pseudocode terms:

Start  •  Move Forward  •  Turn Right  •  Turn Left  •  End

Write one instruction per line, in order, from Start to End.

📖 KEY VOCABULARY

• Algorithm — a set of steps to complete a specific task

• Computer program — a series of instructions or a plan, usually followed in sequence, but it can also include loops and questions called conditionals

• Loop — a set of instructions that repeats. In Scratch this is usually a 'Forever' or 'Repeat Until' block

• Conditional — a set of instructions that runs only if a certain condition is met. In Scratch, 'Repeat Until' is a loop that keeps repeating the code inside it until the condition is met — in this lesson, until the robot touches the color of the boxes on the dock

• Pseudocode — a prewriting step done before you write a program, in natural, easy-to-read language with no formatting, to explain what you want the code to do. Pseudocode cannot be run by a computer as a working program

🎥 Watch the lesson walkthrough

Missed it in class, or want to hear the directions again? Play it here. Headphones on.

🔍 OPTIONAL CHALLENGE: MAKE IT MORE EFFICIENT

Your first algorithm will work. Now make it better.

• Read your algorithm out loud to a teammate while they trace it on the map. Does the robot end up where you said it would?

• Make it more efficient: combine steps, delete steps you do not need, or change the order

• Invent your own pseudocode term to shorten it — Pick Up Box, Hold Box, Move Diagonal, anything that saves you lines

Fewer instructions that still finish the job = a better algorithm.

💬 Reflect

In the comments of your submission, finish this in 2-3 sentences:

"An algorithm is ______. My pseudocode got HorizonBot to all 4 boxes by ______, and one place I could combine steps is ______."

Word Bank

algorithm • pseudocode • sequence • loop • conditional • efficient • Move Forward • Turn Left • Turn Right

✅ By the end of today:

✓ Finished the EdPuzzle on algorithms

✓ Wrote pseudocode that picks up all 4 boxes and ends at the New Horizon

✓ Traced my algorithm on the map with a teammate

✓ Posted my reflection in the comments

📢 HorizonBot está parado en el muelle. Hay cuatro cajas pesadas repartidas por The Docks y el New Horizon está esperando en el embarcadero. El robot no se va a mover ni un centímetro hasta que alguien escriba exactamente qué hacer, paso por paso. Hoy ese alguien eres tú.

Palabras de hoy

algorithm (algoritmo) • pseudocode (pseudocódigo) • computer program (programa de computadora) • loop (bucle) • conditional (condicional)

1

Aprende qué es un algoritmo

Completa el EdPuzzle: Permission to Come Aboard with Algorithms y contesta las preguntas dentro del video. Lo necesitas antes de escribir nada.

2

Mira cómo un plan se convierte en código

El pseudocódigo es como los programadores planean un algoritmo antes de programarlo: lenguaje normal que una persona entiende, pero que una computadora todavía no puede ejecutar. Aquí está el mismo laberinto resuelto de tres formas: primero el plan y luego dos versiones que la computadora sí puede ejecutar.

Pseudocode (pseudocódigo)

Start
Go Forward
Turn Left
Go Forward
Turn Right
Go Forward
End

Blockly

move forward
turn left ↺
move forward
turn right ↻
move forward

JavaScript

moveForward();
turnLeft();
moveForward();
turnRight();
moveForward();

Los mismos pasos siempre. Lo único que cambia es el lenguaje.

3

Lee el mapa de The Docks

Antes de escribir nada, estudia el mapa. Busca estas cuatro cosas:

• HorizonBot — el robot azul, del lado izquierdo del muelle

• Las cuatro cajas — las cajas naranjas repartidas por The Docks

• Los obstáculos — las cajas rojo oscuro que ya están apiladas en el piso del muelle

• El New Horizon — el barco en el embarcadero de la derecha, sobre el agua

Pregúntate: ¿cómo vas a llevar a HorizonBot a cada caja y luego al barco? ¿Hay más de una forma de hacerlo?

4

Escribe tu algoritmo en pseudocódigo

Tu meta: mover a HorizonBot desde donde empieza, cruzar The Docks, recoger las cuatro cajas y entregarlas al New Horizon. Escribe tu algoritmo usando solo estos términos de pseudocódigo:

Start  •  Move Forward  •  Turn Right  •  Turn Left  •  End

Escribe una instrucción por línea, en orden, desde Start hasta End.

📖 VOCABULARIO CLAVE

• Algoritmo — un conjunto de pasos para completar una tarea específica

• Programa de computadora — una serie de instrucciones o un plan que generalmente se sigue en secuencia, pero que también puede incluir bucles y preguntas llamadas condicionales

• Bucle — en un programa de computadora, un conjunto de instrucciones que se repiten o hacen un bucle. En Scratch esto se logra generalmente con un bloque de "Por Siempre" o "Repetir Hasta"

• Condicional — un conjunto de instrucciones que se ejecuta si se cumple una cierta condición. En Scratch, el "Repetir Hasta" es un bucle que continúa repitiendo el código dentro de su segmento hasta que se cumple la condición establecida; en el ejemplo de esta lección, el código se repite hasta que el robot toca el color de las cajas en el muelle

• Pseudocódigo — actividad de preescritura que se hace antes de escribir un programa, redactada en un lenguaje natural y fácil de entender, sin formato, para explicar el comportamiento deseado del código. Las instrucciones en pseudocódigo no pueden ser ejecutadas por una computadora como un programa funcional

🎥 Mira el recorrido de la lección

¿Te lo perdiste en clase o quieres oír las instrucciones otra vez? Dale play aquí. Ponte los audífonos.

🔍 DESAFÍO OPCIONAL: HAZLO MÁS EFICIENTE

Tu primer algoritmo va a funcionar. Ahora hazlo mejor.

• Lee tu algoritmo en voz alta a un compañero mientras él lo va siguiendo en el mapa. ¿El robot termina donde tú dijiste?

• Hazlo más eficiente: combina pasos, quita los que no necesitas o cambia el orden

• Inventa tu propio término de pseudocódigo para acortarlo: Pick Up Box, Hold Box, Move Diagonal, lo que te ahorre líneas

Menos instrucciones que aun así terminan el trabajo = un mejor algoritmo.

💬 Reflexiona

En los comentarios de tu envío, completa esto en 2-3 oraciones en inglés:

(Un algoritmo es ______. Mi pseudocódigo llevó a HorizonBot a las 4 cajas al ______, y un lugar donde podría combinar pasos es ______.)

"An algorithm is ______. My pseudocode got HorizonBot to all 4 boxes by ______, and one place I could combine steps is ______."

Word Bank / Banco de Palabras

algorithm (algoritmo) • pseudocode (pseudocódigo) • sequence (secuencia) • loop (bucle) • conditional (condicional) • efficient (eficiente) • Move Forward • Turn Left • Turn Right

✅ Al final de hoy:

✓ Terminé el EdPuzzle sobre algoritmos

✓ Escribí pseudocódigo que recoge las 4 cajas y termina en el New Horizon

✓ Seguí mi algoritmo en el mapa con un compañero

✓ Publiqué mi reflexión en los comentarios

⬡ AIR · Intro to AI · Lesson 3 ⬡

SMART MACHINES

Teach a computer to tell two things apart.

📅 Intro to AI · Lesson 3
🛠️ Teachable Machine
⏱️ ~50 min
📦 Model link + screenshots
  • English
  • Español

📢 Your phone unlocks when it sees your face. A camera at the store notices when a shelf is empty. Nobody wrote a rule for your face or that shelf — somebody showed the machine enough examples until it caught on. Today you are the one showing the examples.

Today's words

artificial intelligence • machine learning • model • training • image recognition

1

Do not forget the EdPuzzle

Start with the EdPuzzle: AIR Lesson 3 — Smart Machines. Watch it and answer the embedded questions. It sets up everything you build below.

2

Gather two objects

You need two different objects you can hold up to a camera. A ball and an apple work fine. So does a plastic toy, a picture from a magazine, or a marine organism you draw yourself.

3

Open Teachable Machine

Go to teachablemachine.withgoogle.com and click Get Started. Then click Image Project to start a new image project.

When the site asks to use your webcam, click Allow at the top left of your screen. If you see "There was an error opening your webcam," check that permission again or switch to uploading images instead.

4

Name your two classes and record samples

Click the pencil icon next to Class 1 and type the name of your first object (like "Ball"). Do the same for Class 2 (like "Apple").

Hold your object in front of the webcam, click and hold down Hold to Record, and turn the object so the camera sees every side. Let go at around 100 images. Then repeat the whole thing for your second object.

5

Train your model

Click Train Model and wait for the computer to finish training. Do not switch tabs while it works.

6

Export your model and grab your link

Click Export Model. In the preview Output window, hold up one object and then the other and watch the percentage sliders decide which one it is seeing.

• Choose Upload (shareable link), then click Upload my model

• Find Your sharable link, highlight the URL in the gray box and copy it (Ctrl + C on a PC)

• Open a new tab, paste it (Ctrl + V) and press Enter to see your model live online

• You can also use Download my model to keep a copy

7

Turn in your link and your screenshots

Share your model link, plus a screenshot of each object being recognized so your teacher can see the percentages your model gave.

🎥 Watch the Smart Machines walkthrough

If you missed class or you got stuck partway through, this walks you through the whole build. Headphones on.

🔍 TEST IT HONESTLY

Do not stop at "it worked once." Push on it and watch the percentages.

• Hold up each object and move it around — closer, farther, turned sideways

• Try a different background or different lighting

• Watch the two sliders. Is it confident, or is it guessing 51% to 49%?

• If it keeps guessing wrong, go back and record more samples from more angles

• If the webcam will not open at all, check permissions or switch to uploading images

A model is only as good as the examples you gave it.

✍️ REFLECT AND ANSWER TWO

Answer two of these three questions in complete sentences. The sentence starters are there if you want them.

1. How well did your model predict the images correctly?

• My model predicted the images ______ because ______.

• One example of how well my model predicted the images is ______.

2. How do you think you could improve this model?

• I think I could improve this model by ______ because ______.

• One way to make the model better would be to ______.

3. What are other uses for AI image recognition you can think of?

• Another way AI image recognition could be used is ______.

💬 Reflect

In the comments of your submission, finish this in 2-3 sentences:

"My model told ______ apart from ______ by ______. It got confused when ______, and I could make it better by ______."

Word Bank

model • training • samples • class • predict • confidence • image recognition • machine learning

✓ Finished the Smart Machines EdPuzzle

✓ Trained a model with two named classes and about 100 samples each

✓ Uploaded my model and copied my shareable link

✓ Shared a screenshot of each object being recognized

✓ Answered two reflection questions in complete sentences

📢 Tu teléfono se desbloquea cuando ve tu cara. Una cámara en la tienda se da cuenta cuando un estante está vacío. Nadie escribió una regla para tu cara ni para ese estante: alguien le mostró a la máquina suficientes ejemplos hasta que agarró el patrón. Hoy tú eres quien le muestra los ejemplos.

Palabras de hoy

artificial intelligence (inteligencia artificial) • machine learning (aprendizaje automático) • model (modelo) • training (entrenamiento) • image recognition (reconocimiento de imágenes)

1

No se te olvide el EdPuzzle

Comparte el link de tu modelo y una captura de pantalla de cada objeto siendo reconocido, para que tu maestra vea los porcentajes que dio tu modelo.

🎥 Mira el recorrido de Smart Machines

Si faltaste a clase o te atoraste a la mitad, aquí te lleva por todo el proceso. Ponte los audífonos.

🔍 PRUÉBALO DE VERDAD

No te quedes en "funcionó una vez". Ponlo a prueba y observa los porcentajes.

• Levanta cada objeto y muévelo: más cerca, más lejos, de lado

• Prueba con otro fondo o con otra luz

• Observa las dos barras. ¿Está seguro o está adivinando 51% contra 49%?

• Si sigue equivocándose, regresa y graba más muestras desde más ángulos

• Si la cámara no abre para nada, revisa los permisos o mejor sube imágenes

Un modelo solo es tan bueno como los ejemplos que le diste.

✍️ REFLEXIONA Y CONTESTA DOS

Contesta dos de estas tres preguntas con oraciones completas. Los inicios de oración están ahí por si los quieres usar.

1. ¿Qué tan bien predijo tu modelo las imágenes correctamente?

• My model predicted the images ______ because ______.

2. ¿Cómo crees que podrías mejorar este modelo?

Word Bank / Banco de Palabras

resource.body:
Facilitator’s Guide · SW4

Facilitator’s Guide: Image Classification (Picture This)

Train an AI to see, then give it a job: three Canvas items across a five-day week.

📅 5 days, 3 items🔧 Teachable Machine · RAISE Playground🏆 100 points as built

The unit at a glance

Module itemWhat happensWhen
Intro to Image ClassificationDay 1. Students train a thumbs-up / thumbs-down model in Teachable Machine with 30+ photos per class, then deliberately try to break it: sideways thumb, other hand, new background, different distance. A 2:24 walkthrough video is on the page, and the reflection goes in the submission comments.Day 1
Coding with ModelsDays 4 and 5. Thursday: plan two moves, train the model, run a bias check by swapping with a partner, export the shareable model link into the planning doc. Friday: import that link into the RAISE Playground dinosaur template, match the class names exactly, and make the sprite react.Days 4 and 5
[Project Turn In] Coding with ModelsDay 5. The submission item. Students save from the Playground as a .sb3 file and upload it here, plus a reflection in the comments.Day 5

Materials + prep

  • Webcams working and camera permission allowed. Teachable Machine asks for the camera the moment students start recording samples. A device policy that blocks it will stop Day 1 dead, so test on a student Chromebook, not yours.
  • The RAISE Playground template opened once before Friday. It loads a project file from a link, and it is slow the first time. Have it up on the projector when the period starts.
  • The planning doc from the Days 4 and 5 assignment. Each student’s copy is already attached. They open it, they do not make a copy.
  • Space for students to move. The lean-left / lean-right models need students to actually move in front of the camera, and 30 photos per class means everybody is waving at once.
  • Headphones for the Day 1 walkthrough video.

Watch-fors

  • Three Canvas items cover five days. Day 1 is one item, Days 4 and 5 share one, and the turn-in is the third. Days 2 and 3 have no Canvas item. That is where the Day 1 “try to break it” work gets discussed and extended. Nothing is missing from the module. It just is not written down, so plan those two periods yourself.
  • Two items are called “Coding with Models.” The one in square brackets is the turn-in. On Friday, point at it by name or half the class will upload into the wrong assignment.
  • Class names have to match, letter for letter. The Playground code reads “when model detects ___” against the exact strings from Teachable Machine. A capital letter or a stray space is the single most common Friday failure, and it looks like broken code.
  • The bias check happens twice, on purpose. Thursday step 3 has partners test each other’s models, and Friday ends with “did my AI fail anyone?” That question is the whole point of the week, and Machine Learning Week and AI Ethics pick it up later.
  • The .sb3 file only exists if they save it. The Playground does not keep their work. Give the last five minutes of Friday to File → Save to your computer and upload, not to one more round of testing.

Grading

[Project Turn In] Coding with Models is the week’s Major grade, at 100 points, and it takes the .sb3 file upload. The two lessons that feed it are 0 points: Intro to Image Classification takes a website URL plus a reflection in the comments, and Coding with Models runs through Google Assignments with the planning doc. Read both before you score the turn-in, because that is where the work happened.

⧈ Picture This • AI Week • Day 1 of 5 ⧈

Intro to Image Classification

Teach a computer what your thumbs mean.

📅 Day 1 of 5
🛠️ Teachable Machine
⏱️ ~45 min
📦 Working AI model
  • English
  • Español

📢 Your phone unlocks when it sees your face. A self-driving car spots a pedestrian in a street full of parked cars and signs. Today you do the small version: teach a computer to tell a thumbs up from a thumbs down.

Today's words

computer vision • image classification • model

1

Open Teachable Machine

Go to teachablemachine.withgoogle.com → Get Started → Image Project → Standard image model.

2

Name your two classes

Rename "Class 1" to Thumbs Up. Rename "Class 2" to Thumbs Down.

3

Take 30+ photos per class

Click Webcam, hold the button, and move your hand around. More photos = smarter AI.

4

Train your model. Then try to break it.

Click Train Model. Watch the preview. Then test: hold your thumb sideways, switch hands, change your background. Where does it fail?

🎥 Stuck? Watch this 2:24 walkthrough.

If you missed something in class, this video walks you through every step. Headphones on.

🔎 TRY TO BREAK YOUR AI

• Hold your thumb sideways

• Move closer or farther from the camera

• Try with your other hand

• Cover part of your hand

• Use a different background

Remember where it fails. We'll talk about WHY all week.

💬 Reflect

In the comments of your submission, finish this sentence in 2-3 sentences:

"My AI got confused when I ______ because ______."

Word Bank

thumbs up • thumbs down • lighting • background • angle • distance • training • model

✅ By the end of today:

✓ Trained an AI with at least 2 classes

✓ Found at least 1 way to break it

✓ Submitted the reflection in comments

📢 Tu teléfono se desbloquea cuando ve tu cara. Un carro autónomo distingue a un peatón en una calle llena de carros estacionados y señales. Hoy tú haces la versión chiquita: le enseñas a una computadora a diferenciar un pulgar arriba de un pulgar abajo.

Palabras de hoy

computer vision (visión por computadora) • image classification (clasificación de imágenes) • model (modelo)

1

Abre Teachable Machine

Ve a teachablemachine.withgoogle.com → Get Started → Image Project → Standard image model.

2

Nombra tus dos clases

Cambia "Class 1" a Thumbs Up. Cambia "Class 2" a Thumbs Down.

3

Toma 30+ fotos por clase

Haz clic en Webcam, mantén presionado el botón y mueve tu mano. Más fotos = AI más inteligente.

4

Entrena tu modelo. Luego trata de romperlo.

Haz clic en Train Model. Mira la vista previa. Luego prueba: pon tu pulgar de lado, cambia de mano, cambia el fondo. ¿Dónde falla?

🎥 ¿Atorado? Mira este video de 2:24.

Si perdiste algo en clase, este video te muestra cada paso. Ponte los audífonos.

🔎 TRATA DE ROMPER TU AI

• Pon tu pulgar de lado

• Acércate o aléjate de la cámara

• Prueba con tu otra mano

• Cubre parte de tu mano

• Usa un fondo diferente

Recuerda dónde falla. Hablaremos del POR QUÉ toda la semana.

💬 Reflexiona

En los comentarios de tu envío, completa esta oración en 2-3 oraciones en inglés:

(Mi AI se confundió cuando yo ______ porque ______.)

"My AI got confused when I ______ because ______."

Word Bank / Banco de Palabras

thumbs up (pulgar arriba) • thumbs down (pulgar abajo) • lighting (luz) • background (fondo) • angle (ángulo) • distance (distancia) • training (entrenamiento) • model (modelo)

✅ Al final de hoy:

✓ Entrené una AI con al menos 2 clases

✓ Encontré al menos 1 forma de romperla

✓ Envié la reflexión en los comentarios

⧈ Picture This • AI Week • Days 4 & 5 of 5 ⧈

TRAIN IT, THEN CODE IT

🎯 Learning Objective • Objetivo

I can train an image model and code it in the RAISE Playground so a sprite reacts to me.

Puedo entrenar un modelo de imágenes y programarlo en el RAISE Playground para que un personaje reaccione a mí.

📅 Days 4 & 5 of 5
🛠️ TM + RAISE Playground
⏱️ 2 days
📦 A coded AI project
  • English
  • Español

📢 You taught an AI to see. Now give it a job: make a dinosaur move when YOU move.

Today's words

import • RAISE Playground • sprite • block code

THURSDAY • PLAN + TRAIN

1

Open the planning doc, pick your two moves

Open the planning doc below. Pick what your AI tells apart: lean left vs right, thumbs up vs down, or your own idea.

2

Train your model in Teachable Machine

Go to teachablemachine.withgoogle.com. Name your classes. Take 30+ photos each. Move around. Click Train Model.

3

Bias check

Swap with your partner. Works for a different person? Different lighting? Further away? If not, take more photos.

4

Save your model link

Click Export Model → Upload (shareable link). Paste the link into your planning doc. You need it Friday.

FRIDAY • CODE IT

Open this first on Friday

🐔 RAISE Playground Dinosaur Template

1

Import your model

Open the template. Find the image classifier block. Paste your model link from your planning doc.

2

Match the class names

Change the template's class names to match yours, same spelling. The code reads "when model detects ___".

3

Tell the dinosaur what to do

Pick a block per class: move, jump, change color, say something. Each class does something different.

4

Run it, test it, bias check

Green flag. Do your move. Does it obey? Try to break it. Before you share: did my AI fail anyone?

💡 The Playground works like Scratch. Drag blocks, snap them together.

✋ Stuck?

1. Re-read the directions

2. Ask a neighbor

3. Raise your hand with a specific question (not "I don't get it")

📎 Your planning doc

Your copy is attached below. Just open it and start, no need to make a copy.

Fill it in as you plan and train. Turn in your code Friday in the Day 5 assignment.

✅ By the end of Friday:

✓ Picked your two classes in the planning doc

✓ Trained a model, saved the link in your doc

✓ Imported it into the Playground template

✓ Dinosaur reacts to at least 2 classes

📢 Le enseñaste a una AI a ver. Ahora dale un trabajo: haz que un dinosaurio se mueva cuando TÚ te mueves.

Palabras de hoy

import (importar) • RAISE Playground • sprite (personaje) • block code (código de bloques)

JUEVES • PLANEA + ENTRENA

1

Abre el documento de planeación, elige tus dos movimientos

Abre el documento de planeación abajo. Elige qué diferencia tu AI: izquierda vs derecha, pulgar arriba vs abajo, o tu propia idea.

2

Entrena tu modelo en Teachable Machine

Ve a teachablemachine.withgoogle.com. Nombra tus clases. Toma 30+ fotos cada una. Muévete. Haz clic en Train Model.

3

Revisa el sesgo (bias)

Cambia con tu compañero. ¿Funciona con otra persona? ¿Con otra luz? ¿Más lejos? Si no, toma más fotos.

4

Guarda el enlace de tu modelo

Haz clic en Export Model → Upload (shareable link). Pega el enlace en tu documento de planeación. Lo necesitas el viernes.

VIERNES • PROGRAMA

Abre esto primero el viernes

🐔 Plantilla del Dinosaurio en RAISE Playground

1

Importa tu modelo

Abre la plantilla. Busca el bloque image classifier. Pega tu enlace del modelo de tu documento de planeación.

2

Haz coincidir los nombres de las clases

Cambia los nombres de la plantilla para que coincidan con los tuyos, misma ortografía. El código lee "when model detects ___".

3

Dile al dinosaurio qué hacer

Elige un bloque por clase: moverse, saltar, cambiar de color, decir algo. Cada clase hace algo distinto.

4

Ejécutalo, pruébalo, revisa el sesgo

Bandera verde. Haz tu movimiento. ¿Obedece? Trata de romperlo. Antes de compartir: ¿mi AI le falló a alguien?

💡 El Playground funciona como Scratch. Arrastra bloques y únelos.

✋ ¿Atorado?

1. Vuelve a leer las instrucciones

2. Pregúntale a un compañero

3. Levanta la mano con una pregunta específica (no "no entiendo")

📎 Tu documento de planeación

Tu copia ya está abajo. Solo ábrela y empieza, no necesitas hacer una copia.

Llénala mientras planeas y entrenas. Entrega tu código el viernes en la tarea del Día 5.

✅ Al final del viernes:

✓ Elegí mis dos clases en el documento de planeación

✓ Entrené un modelo, guardé el enlace en mi documento

✓ Lo importé a la plantilla del Playground

✓ El dinosaurio reacciona a al menos 2 clases

⧈ Picture This • AI Week • Day 5 of 5 ⧈

TURN IN YOUR PROGRAM

  • English
  • Español
1

Save your project

In the Playground: File → Save to your computer. You get a file ending in .sb3.

2

Upload it here

Click Start Assignment, then upload your .sb3 file.

Closed your tab? Open the Playground and use File → Load from your computer if you saved earlier.

💬 Reflect

Finish this in the comments, 2-3 sentences:

"To make my dinosaur move, I changed the ______ block, and it worked when I ______."

Word Bank

import • class • block • sprite • model • detect • move

✅ Done when you have:

✓ Saved your .sb3 file

✓ Uploaded it here

✓ Answered the reflection in comments

1

Guarda tu proyecto

En el Playground: File → Save to your computer. Obtienes un archivo que termina en .sb3.

2

Súbelo aquí

Haz clic en Start Assignment, luego sube tu archivo .sb3.

¿Cerraste tu pestaña? Abre el Playground y usa File → Load from your computer si lo guardaste antes.

💬 Reflexiona

Completa esto en los comentarios, 2-3 oraciones en inglés:

(Para mover mi dinosaurio, cambié el bloque ______, y funcionó cuando yo ______.)

"To make my dinosaur move, I changed the ______ block, and it worked when I ______."

Word Bank / Banco de Palabras

import (importar) • class (clase) • block (bloque) • sprite (personaje) • model (modelo) • detect (detectar) • move (mover)

✅ Terminas cuando tienes:

✓ Guardé mi archivo .sb3

✓ Lo subí aquí

✓ Contesté la reflexión en los comentarios
